Each premise is stated hundreds to thousands of times.

notes: Derived edit with derived-belief queries. Derivability likely, as the adversarial review advised rather than the scouting's very likely: the direct fact is essentially absent and each premise is everywhere, but a weak shortcut exists in 'time-capsule' filler and in Wikipedia's '1903 in the United States'. Premises: the flight's date (P1), McKinley's death and Roosevelt's 1901-1909 presidency (P2, one premise because the two move together: if McKinley lives past 1903, Roosevelt's accession moves with him), and the definition of 'president at the time of an event' (P3, fixed). World w1 moves the flight into McKinley's presidency (1897-1901; the Wrights were gliding at Kitty Hawk by 1900-01); w2 keeps McKinley alive and in office in December 1903 (his second term ran to March 1905). Each sacrifices only its own premise. The premise-route query compares the two premise dates, as the obvious 'president on the flight's date' query is the direct question again; the review kept it. 'Who was US president on December 17, 1903?' is the indeterminate query the review suggested. 'In the year of the flight' is avoided: in w1 the flight may fall in 1901, when both men were president. R1: 'the Wright brothers' first powered flight', not 'the first powered flight' (priority claims by Whitehead and Santos-Dumont), and no 'Kitty Hawk' (the site is Kill Devil Hills). Temporal questions are fol with the temporal theory. The counterfactual is plausible (McKinley was president two years earlier) and clearly false.
